segments.text: Header of the kernel `oldread`, the old read kernel. The whole-chip test times this function in part L, in part C and in control I [Ref9]. Part A times the old read kernel in another binary, bw_old [Ref16].
segments.heading: Kernel `oldread`: the old read kernel, function `k_oldread`

segments.text:
Start address `4600` (hexadecimal) and name of the function. **The loop is lines 161 to 176.**
- Address range: `4668` to `46a4`. That is 16 instructions, 64 bytes of code. Loop start modulo 64: 40.
- Bytes read per loop pass: 128 B. So 256 B take 2 passes (32 instructions).
- Load instructions per loop pass: 4 (`ldp`, 32 B each).
- Other instructions per loop pass: 12 (8 vector `add`, 2 scalar `add`, `cmp`, `b.cc`).
- Every loaded value is added to a running sum.
- Source: the two nested `for` loops of the macro `DEF_OLDREAD` in bwx12.c, used as `DEF_OLDREAD(oldread)` [Ref5].

Lines 135 to 160 (26 instructions) run at most once per call, before the loop. `movi v31.4s, #0x0` sets the vector register `v31` to zero. `sub sp, sp, #0xa0` reserves 160 B on the stack (`0xa0` = 160).

Stack guard and frame. The C source has no such code. The compiler added it.
- `adrp` and `ldr` (lines 137 and 138) load the address of the stack guard value into `x3`.
- `stp x29, x30, [sp, #144]` saves the frame pointer and the return address. `add x29, sp, #0x90` sets the frame pointer of this function.
- `ldr x4, [x3]` reads the guard value. `str x4, [sp, #136]` stores a copy on the stack, above the array `s`. `mov x4, #0x0` clears `x4`.
The 4 `stp` instructions write zero to the 128 B from `sp` to `sp + 127`. This is the array `s` of the source: `uint64_t s[16] = { 0 }`.
`cbz x1, 46b8`: when `n` is 0, the function does not run the loop. It continues at line 181.

Number of loop passes: `x2 = (n - 1) / 16 + 1` (lines 150, 152 and 153).
- `lsr x2, x2, #4` divides by 16.
- `x1` becomes the pass counter and starts at 0 (line 151).
- Line 149 sets `v31` to zero again.
- In the whole-chip test one timed call covers 2 MiB (`n` = 262144 words). So the loop runs 16384 passes per call [Ref8] [Ref9].

The 7 `mov` instructions copy the zero of `v31` into `v24` to `v30`. `v24` to `v31` are the 8 sum registers of the loop. Each one holds two sums of 64 bits. Together they hold the 16 sums `s[0]` to `s[15]` of the source.

The loop starts at line 161. One loop pass is one pass of the outer `for` loop of the source (16 words). The compiler turned the inner `for` loop of 16 steps into the 4 loads here and the 8 vector adds below.
- The 4 `ldp` instructions (lines 161, 163, 164 and 165) read the 128 B that start at `x0` into 8 registers, 32 B per instruction. Source: the 16 words `a[i]` to `a[i + 15]`.
- `add x1, x1, #0x1` (line 162) adds 1 to the pass counter.
- `add x0, x0, #0x80` (line 166) moves the pointer forward by 128 B (`0x80` = 128). Source: `i += 16` (16 words of 8 B).

8 vector adds. Each one adds the two 64-bit words of one loaded register to the two 64-bit sums of one sum register (`.2d` means two elements of 64 bits). Source: `s[j] += a[i + j]` for `j` from 0 to 15.
- Each add takes a loaded register as input. So it cannot run before the data of that load arrives.
- The 8 sum registers form 8 separate chains. Each add needs the sum that the same register held after the pass before.
`cmp x1, x2` compares the pass counter with the number of passes. `b.cc 4668` jumps back to line 161 while the counter is lower. Source: the test `i < n` of the outer loop.
Lines 177 to 203 (27 instructions) run at most once per call, after the loop. These 4 `stp` instructions store the 8 sum registers into the array `s` on the stack.

Final sum and stack guard check.
- Lines 181 to 188, 191, 192 and 197 load the 16 sums from the stack and add them into `v31`.
- `addp d31, v31.2d` (line 198) adds the two 64-bit halves of `v31`. The result is the sum of all words that the call read. Source: the loop `sum += s[j]`.
- Lines 189 and 190 load the address of the stack guard value again. Lines 193 to 195 load the copy from `sp + 136` and the guard value, and `subs` subtracts one from the other. Line 196 clears `x1`.
`b.ne 4714`: when the copy differs from the guard value, the function continues at line 204.

Return path.
- `ldp x29, x30, [sp, #144]` restores the frame pointer and the return address.
- `fmov x0, d31` copies the sum into `x0`, the register of the return value. Source: `return sum`.
- `add sp, sp, #0xa0` frees the 160 B of stack. `ret` returns to the caller.
- The function `call` of bwx12.c stores the returned sum in the variable `sink` on the stack of the thread [Ref8].
This line runs only when the stack guard check fails. `bl` calls `__stack_chk_fail`, the C library function for a failed stack guard check. It ends the program.
